title: Edmund and the Promise
premise: Odile Okonkwo built her wedding-planning empire on the belief that love is a performance she no longer performs—especially not with Edmund Reyes, the photographer who broke her heart a decade ago and now shows up contracted to shoot the biggest wedding of her career. A snowstorm traps them in a shuttered Catskills estate with the bride and groom's secrets, forcing Odile and Edmund to confront the promise they made at twenty-two: that if they ever met again, they'd tell each other the whole truth. As the storm buries the venue, Odile discovers Edmund has been quietly buying back every photograph he ever took of her, protecting her from a scandal tied to his powerful family—and that forgiving him means first forgiving herself for walking away. The book ends when the storm clears: Odile chooses to plan one last wedding, her own, on the condition that this time there are no promises, only presence.
about_author: Mara Okafor is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent six years watching other people's vows before writing her own stories. She lives between Lagos and Lisbon, where she collects unsent letters and photographs of empty ballrooms.

chapters.title: The Muscle Memory of Hearts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She runs a flawless society wedding while privately cataloguing all the ways love fails, establishing her creed that the heart is trainable. When she learns the photographer for her next commission is Edmund Reyes, her hands shake for the first time in years. Emotional beat: controlled dread beneath polished competence.

chapters.title: Contract Terms
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He accepts the Ashford estate wedding knowing Odile will be there, telling himself it's closure he needs professionally. We learn he left her ten years ago without explanation after his family intervened. Emotional beat: guilt dressed up as strategy.

chapters.title: The Bride Who Hired Both of Them
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Client Vivienne Ashford reveals she deliberately booked both Odile and Edmund because she read an old profile about them as 'the couple who planned weddings but never had one.' Odile nearly walks out; the fee keeps her. Emotional beat: humiliation sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Unsent Letters
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the drive north, both rehearse what they'll say. Flashbacks surface: a rooftop in their twenties, a promise to always tell the truth, and the night Edmund vanished. Emotional beat: nostalgia curdling into resentment.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They arrive early to prep the estate; the forecast turns, and by midnight the roads close. Stranded staff evacuate; only Odile, Edmund, Vivienne, and groom Theo remain. Emotional beat: claustrophobia and unwanted intimacy.

chapters.title: Candlelight Inventory
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Power fails. By generator light, Edmund photographs the empty ballroom and catches Odile dancing alone to remembered music—the same song from their rooftop. She sees him watching. Emotional beat: tenderness ambushing old anger.

chapters.title: The First Truth
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Cornered by the storm, Edmund admits his father threatened to destroy Odile's fledgling career if he stayed with her. She doesn't believe him—or refuses to. Emotional beat: the past cracking open.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Secret
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV (brief). Vivienne confesses to Odile that she's marrying Theo for stability, not love, and asks how Odile plans weddings for people who don't believe. Odile gives advice she doesn't follow. Emotional beat: mirrored self-deception.

chapters.title: The Archive Box
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Odile finds a box of Edmund's prints: every photograph he ever took of her, plus receipts showing he's spent years buying negatives from clients to keep them private. Emotional beat: evidence of devotion she can't weaponize.

chapters.title: What I Did Instead of Missing You
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She retaliates with her own confession: she didn't wait—she married briefly, badly, and built her business on proving Edmund wrong. Emotional beat: pride exposed as armor.

chapters.title: Theo Walks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo discovers Vivienne's doubts via a misdelivered note and tries to leave through the snow; Edmund stops him at the treeline. The stranded group fractures. Emotional beat: the wedding Odile must save is dissolving.

chapters.title: Negotiating with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile calls her ex-husband from the landline, seeking absolution, and gets none—he tells her she left him long before the papers. Emotional beat: the person in the mirror comes into focus.

chapters.title: Edmund's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He reveals the full scope of his family's power: his father's firm bankrolled half of Odile's early clients, meaning her success was both sabotaged and secretly subsidized. Emotional beat: betrayal complicated by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Promise Clause
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They find the old letter they wrote at twenty-two—a sealed promise to tell the truth if they ever met again. Reading it aloud together becomes the book's quiet turning point. Emotional beat: grief shared instead of traded.

chapters.title: Thaw Lines
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A fragile truce: they rebuild the wedding together through the night, arguing like partners again, laughing despite themselves. Vivienne watches them and makes a decision of her own. Emotional beat: warmth without permission.

chapters.title: The Father Arrives
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Roads partially clear; Edmund's father arrives uninvited, intending to buy the Ashford estate and bury the scandal. He offers Odile money to walk away from Edmund publicly. Emotional beat: power showing its true face.

chapters.title: Refusal in Front of Witnesses
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile declines—not for Edmund, but for herself—and exposes the family's interference to Vivienne and Theo. Climactic confrontation where she stops being invisible. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into self-possession.

chapters.title: Snowmelt
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund confronts his father, renouncing the inheritance and the archive's protection, choosing truth over safety. Father disowns him; Edmund feels lighter than expected. Emotional beat: liberation at a cost.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Almost Wasn't
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Vivienne and Theo marry honestly—small, imperfect, real—in the half-flooded ballroom. Odile plans it flawlessly and cries during the vows. Emotional beat: belief returning against her will.

chapters.title: Time Already Running Out
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With the storm gone, departure looms. Edmund is offered a job abroad; Odile assumes history repeats. Neither says stay. Emotional beat: the old pattern threatening to win.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Alone in the emptied estate, Odile finally forgives herself—for leaving, for the marriage, for hiding behind other people's love. She drives to Edmund's departure gate not to stop him but to speak plainly. Emotional beat: forgiveness as action, not feeling.

chapters.title: No Promises, Only Presence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Edmund misses the flight. Epilogue a year later: they co-found a studio planning small, honest ceremonies; the final scene is their own courthouse wedding with no vows written in advance. Emotional beat: belonging chosen daily rather than promised once.
